name: Hu tieu My Tho
summary: Mỹ Tho’s rice-noodle bowl comes dry, the strands tossed with pork crackling, fried shallot, and soy under minced pork, or wet, with sliced pork, liver, shrimp, squid, and quail egg under the broth. A good strand smells of rice and stays soft without going mushy or sour.
origin: Mỹ Tho, from strands of fragrant Gò Cát rice made in phường Mỹ Phong.
history: The provincial tourism portal dates the bowl’s fame to the early 1960s, from carts between Mỹ Tho and Gò Công, and records a 2014 listing as a dish of Asian culinary value. The national tourism site also starts in the 1960s and names the cooks Phánh Ký, Tuyền Ký, and Nam Sơn.

Vietnam Tourism’s noodle-village article reaches back to Hoa cooks at the end of the 19th century. The city portal claims a hundred years and records a cooperative in 2007 and a brand certificate for “Hủ tiếu Mỹ Tho” in December 2008.
culture: Mỹ Tho eats it at breakfast, lunch, and supper. It is its own bowl, not hủ tiếu Nam Vang, hủ tiếu Tàu, phở, or bún bò Huế.
The national tourism site serves it with bean sprouts, lime, chili, and soy, and without lettuce, vinegar, or a herb plate. Vietnam Tourism’s village article does put fresh greens on the soup bowl.
texture: The strand should smell of rice and stay soft without turning mushy or sour, so it is blanched only briefly.
taste: You season it yourself from the soy, lime, sugar, and fresh chili or satay on the table.

The provincial portal simmers the broth from pork leg bone, grilled dried squid, cassava root, and spices, and the old phường 9 ward office uses bone, dried squid, dried shrimp, and daikon. Sài Gòn Giải Phóng, 26 Jan 2023, adds marrow bone, spare rib, dried shrimp, and grilled squid.
howToEat: Order it dry, topped with cooked minced pork, or with the broth poured over and finished with spring onion and more crackling.
Add bean sprouts, lime, and chili, then mix the soy, sugar, and satay to your taste.
where: Eat it in the town streets or at the night court. Inside the tourist-boat pier on đường 30 Tháng 4: 18:30–02:00 in a 5 Jan 2019 provincial article, or from 18:00 and busiest 19:00–22:00 on Viet Fun Travel.
Visit ấp Hội Gia in phường Mỹ Phong, open 07:00–18:00, to watch the strands made. The bowl itself is served in town.
seoTitle: Hu tieu My Tho — dry or with broth
seoDescription: Mỹ Tho’s rice-noodle bowl from Gò Cát rice, dry or with broth, at any meal: what goes in, how to season it, and where to eat it on đường 30 Tháng 4.
